purpose: PyTorch deep learning — differentiable HBV-light and LSTM hydrology models

Tensor.detach().numpy().note: Call .detach() before .numpy() on tensors that require gradients. Omitting detach() raises RuntimeError.

DataLoader.note: Set num_workers=0 on macOS/Windows when running inside MCP subprocess to avoid multiprocessing issues.

gotchas: Always call optimizer.zero_grad() before loss.backward() — omitting this accumulates gradients across batches.
NaN in loss usually means exploding gradients. Add gradient clipping: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0).
model.eval() + torch.no_grad() are both required for inference — eval() alone does not stop gradient computation.
torch.save(model.state_dict()) not model itself — loading the full model object breaks across Python versions.
CUDA out-of-memory: reduce batch size or call torch.cuda.empty_cache() then retry. Check torch.cuda.is_available().
Hydrology-specific: streamflow targets often span orders of magnitude — log-transform before training or use NSE loss.
train_hbv_light uses CPU only. Do not move tensors to GPU — HBV-light is small enough that CPU is optimal.
For HBV restarts, re-initialise model parameters (nn.init.uniform_) before each restart, not just the optimizer.

common_patterns.training_loop:
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)
for epoch in range(epochs):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    pred = model(x)
    loss = nse_loss(pred, y)
    loss.backward()
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
    optimizer.step()
